overview: This 509-page file traces U.S. diplomatic assessments of Japan’s finances from 1932 to 1937. Budgets, debt figures, bond issues, and correspondence document the costs of military operations in Manchuria and China, relief spending, yen depreciation, and doubts about Japan’s capacity to fund further expansion. It also includes translated budget schedules, press commentary, and reports on foreign loans.
interest: Translated budgets and diplomatic analyses reveal how officials assessed the financial limits of Japan’s military expansion.
